Max Hoffmann  
Senior ML Engineer | NexaGame Studios  
Amsterdam, Netherlands | +31 6 1234 5678 | max.hoffmann@email.com | linkedin.com/in/maxhoffmann | github.com/max-hoffmann  

Professional Experience  
From 2022 to the present, I’ve served as a Senior ML Engineer at NexaGame Studios, where I focused on integrating AI-driven player behavior analysis into game mechanics. This involved designing scalable models that reduced player churn by 18% in a flagship title. Prior to that, as Lead ML Engineer at PixelForge Interactive (2020–2022), I spearheaded the development of adaptive enemy AI systems, which improved player engagement metrics by 25% across three titles. Before that, my role as Machine Learning Engineer at Virtuoso Games (2018–2020) centered on refining natural language processing pipelines for in-game dialogue systems, achieving a 30% reduction in response latency. My early career included a Data Scientist Internship at LudoLabs (2017), where I contributed to predictive analytics models for player retention.  

Technical Skills  
Docker, GCP, REST API design, MLOps (MLflow/W&B), model deployment, NLP, PyTorch, TensorFlow. My work at NexaGame Studios required deploying PyTorch models to production using MLOps pipelines, while TensorFlow was central to building the NLP models for dialogue systems at Virtuoso Games. I’ve also collaborated on REST API integrations for real-time data streaming, and my experience with GCP has supported cloud-based model training workflows. Docker has been used sparingly for containerizing inference services.  

Education  
Master’s in Machine Learning, TU Delft (2018). Thesis work focused on reinforcement learning applications in dynamic environments, which informed my approach to adaptive AI systems in game development.  

Projects  
At NexaGame Studios, I led the deployment of a player behavior model using PyTorch, which was integrated into the game’s matchmaking system. This required designing an MLOps pipeline with MLflow for tracking experiments and Weights & Biases for monitoring training metrics. At Virtuoso Games, I developed a real-time NLP system for in-game dialogue, combining TensorFlow for sequence modeling with custom rule-based filters to handle edge cases. A separate project at PixelForge Interactive involved creating a recommendation engine for in-game item purchases, leveraging collaborative filtering and deployed via a REST API.  

Languages  
English (native), German (fluent).  

Volunteer / Open Source  
Contributed to an open-source machine learning library for game AI, focusing on modular architecture and compatibility with PyTorch and TensorFlow. Regularly participate in local meetups for game developers and data scientists, sharing insights on model optimization techniques.
